notes: Identity verified independently from the canonical text: title Expected Stock Returns and Variance Risk Premia; authors Tim Bollerslev, George Tauchen, Hao Zhou; doi:10.1093/rfs/hhp008; The Review of Financial Studies v 22 n 11 2009; pages 4463–4492. The supplied text is a primary journal article with methods, results, tables, conclusion, and references, rather than an abstract or secondary account. SOURCE_URL names the authors’ Duke-hosted published-paper PDF. No PDF was supplied, so no rendering performed. Input description and both locators are empty; study_o is null and es_type_o=ser_method does not identify a particular coefficient or standardisation. No candidate was selected using numeric matching or row order. Candidate Table 2 VRP slope coefficients for horizons 1, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 24 months are respectively 0.39, 0.47, 0.30, 0.17, 0.12, 0.11, 0.06, 0.01, with corresponding robust Hodrick t-statistics 1.76, 2.86, 2.15, 1.36, 1.00, 0.94, 0.56, 0.11. These are printed regression slopes, not established standardised effects. Tables 3–6 include additional simple/multiple models and predictors, and Section 3.2 reports alternative variance/volatility definitions. Candidate p evidence: Section 3.1 p.4479 states the monthly positive-slope one-sided test exceeds the 5% significance level; this supports a same-test threshold candidate only, not an exact p or a bound for every horizon. Page 4485 separately states variance-risk-premium coefficients remain statistically significant at the 0.001 level or better in the discussed quarterly specifications; this is not assigned to an unspecified row. No p was computed from t. Candidate sample evidence gives January 1990–December 2007 and monthly regression observations but no target-specific explicit analytic N selected here. The p.4477 n=22 × 78=1716 is a typical month’s five-minute returns used to construct realized variance, not regression N. No calendar count or df-derived N was calculated. All unassigned fields are placeholders.
